newsitem.title: USA: Sierra Leone evacuation of Americans continues.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone evacuation of Americans continues.

text.p: U.S. military helicopters backed by Marines on the ground have evacuated nearly 500 Americans and other foreigners from Sierra Leone to a U.S. warship, the Defence Department said on Friday.
By 10 A.M. EDT (1400 GMT), 467 evacuees -- 227 Americans and 240 third country nationals -- had been taken to the helicopter carrier USS Kearsarge, Pentagon spokeswoman Nancy Burt said.
There were no reports of violence during the evacuation, which followed a coup by army officers in the West African country last weekend.

Burt said CH-53 "Sea Stallion" helicopters, which can carry up to 55 passengers, and CH-46 "Sea Knight" helicopters, capable of taking 24, were being used for the operation, which would probably be completed by the end of the day.
She said evacuated Americans on the Kearsarge would be moved to Conakry, Guinea, about 100 miles (160 km) north of Freetown, and were expected to be flown back from there to the United States.
The Pentagon said 203 U.S. Marines were on the ground in Sierra Leone for security, "administrative processing" and other duties.
